parsed.explanation: The combined regime is High Risk. National entry and document rules are the sharpest traveller-facing exposure: sex assigned at birth governs passports/visas, X markers are not processed for new national documents, and document discrepancies can lead to refusal, secondary scrutiny, or a permanent fraud ineligibility finding. National custody and immigration-detention records include birth-sex placement, forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, sexual abuse, and conversion-style practices. National measures also restrict government-funded facilities and frame trans advocacy within counterterrorism language. The division mitigates somewhat: no statewide adult bathroom ban or adult care ban, and four municipalities protect public accommodations. But statewide nondiscrimination and hate-crime coverage are absent, remedies are partial and contested, and a visitor outside those municipalities has little recourse.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned at birth on passports/visas, do not process new X markers, and treat document discrepancy as possible wilful misrepresentation supporting refusal or permanent fraud ineligibility. Travellers report confiscated or blocked passports and stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; litigation and some court injunctions have blocked or delayed parts of the regime; legal-aid guidance exists.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign visitor’s home passport and visa category meet national adjudication discretion; division-level document-change rules do not protect visitors from national border screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody is documented with forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, and severe sexual abuse against transgender men; national corrections policies impose conversion-style practices and birth-sex custody harms. Detention probability rises with document mismatch or suspected fraud.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some national measures are under challenge or enjoined; limited court review exists, but no effective traveller-facing remedy at the border or in custody is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border discrepancy can escalate from secondary inspection to detention, where national custody rules and conditions govern regardless of division-level protections.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive policy bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; many states impose facility bans, including criminal trespass in some. A documented arrest occurred under a state bathroom law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The division has no statewide adult bathroom or changing-room ban; four municipalities prohibit gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facilities and federally funded settings are governed by the national restriction; division local ordinances do not reach federal buildings, and outside the four municipalities there is no state or local accommodation recourse.

care_services.exposure: National orders target gender-affirming care for minors and restrict funding; the division medical board approved a draft rule treating under-18 transition care as unprofessional conduct. Adult care is not banned statewide.
care_services.protection: The division draft is not yet operative and must pass review and comment; some national orders are enjoined; no statewide adult care ban is documented.
care_services.interaction: An adult visitor faces limited division-level care restriction, but a travelling minor or care-seeking family encounters national and regulatory youth-care exposure; emergency care discovery can still trigger facility and custody rules.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names “radically pro-transgender” groups among priorities, and a justice reward memorandum invokes “radical gender ideology.” The division hate-crime statute omits gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; four municipal ordinances cover public accommodations and employment.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing raises the consequences of outing and may chill police recourse; outside the municipalities, state hate-crime enhancement and nondiscrimination protection are unavailable.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders describe youth transition care as mutilation and direct investigation of schools facilitating social transition; the division education board bars transgender girls from female sports, one district requires birth-sex bathrooms, and the medical board advanced a youth-care restriction.
minors_guardians.protection: The youth-care draft is not in force; some national orders are enjoined; adult care and adult facility use are not banned statewide.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a transgender minor faces national and division regulatory exposure around care, school, and facilities; a visiting minor is less likely to enter local schools but may encounter care and custody rules if detained.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence count or general homicide baseline is supplied, so rate cannot be derived. The division lacks statewide gender-identity hate-crime coverage and nondiscrimination law outside four municipalities.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; four municipal ordinances provide local recourse; no enforcement data for those ordinances is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A victim outside the four municipalities has no state or local bias-crime enhancement or accommodations recourse; police response to trans-specific violence is undocumented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: National entry, facilities, and custody policies remain contested and unevenly applied; division remedies are absent statewide and local ordinances lack documented enforcement. Border fraud findings carry lifetime ineligibility risk.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National litigation has produced injunctions and stays; legal-aid guidance exists; four municipal ordinances and national hate-crime law provide partial paper recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Court relief may block some national measures, but it is slow and incomplete; a traveller at the border or in custody cannot reliably access division-level protections.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar or slightly below. Both feature traveller-facing border/document exclusion. This dossier adds national custody abuse and permanent-ineligibility risk, but it lacks a routine universal entry bar, and the division has no statewide adult bathroom ban.

Below. 0.55-B describes secondary screening and administrative refusal without credible criminal or custody abuse. Here a document discrepancy can trigger fraud-based lifetime ineligibility and detention with documented physical and sexual abuse.

Well below. 0.75-C has trained border officers, brief detention, and working tribunal remedies. This dossier has a hostile national document regime, documented custody harms, and no statewide nondiscrimination or hate-crime recourse outside four municipalities.

Above. 0.25-C has birth-sex custody assaults and a cross-dressing offence. This division lacks an adult facility ban or presentation criminal statute, but national entry and custody exposures keep it in the High Risk band rather than the severe tier.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is driven by national rules that follow the traveller through visa adjudication, border screening, federal facilities, and any detention. Document mismatch or suspicion of misrepresentation can lead to refusal, permanent ineligibility, or custody, where birth-sex placement and documented abuse are severe. The division reduces everyday adult exposure: no statewide adult bathroom or care ban, and four municipalities protect accommodations. But statewide nondiscrimination and hate-crime coverage are missing, local enforcement is undocumented, and national measures remain contested. A trans visitor who is outed faces meaningful risk of exclusion, detention, and institutional harm, partially offset by local protections and court injunctions.
